seedWorldTruths: A First Sacrifice is a COMING-OF-AGE RITE — closest analogue a Bar Mitzvah / quinceañera / confirmation / graduation, NOT a death ritual. At 16 (younger minds are too unformed to wish safely) a youth, after long study and practice, publicly makes their first wish and offers its price to Fate. It can be stern and formal, but when it goes well it ENDS IN CELEBRATION; catastrophe is UNUSUAL — everyone understands the safeguards the way we understand fire drills. Do NOT default to disaster, apocalypse, curses, or world-ending stakes.

First Favored are hired to GUIDE and SUPERVISE the rite — their alignment-sense and powerful wish-strength make them the preferred (and pricier) choice over human or Kwisheen wishcraft scholars. The supervisor reads the alignment of EVERYONE present, above all the wishing youth, ready to HALT and re-align the wish before it can twist.

The supervisor is a SACRIFICIANT (the role): one whose misalignment-sense is honed enough to supervise (the PC is an apprentice Sacrificiant). THE SACRIFICIANT SEAL — worn by whoever supervises, during ANY official First Sacrifice rite: because a supervisor bolstering the youth’s sacrifice with a wish of their OWN would be a ruinous breach, every Sacrificiant is ceremonially SEALED for the rite — a gossamer BAND drawn across the mouth and tied behind the head (just cloth, part of their ceremonial sash; NO orb, NO bead, NO gag), so they cannot cleanly voice a wish while officiating. Vestments are otherwise the same sheer gossamer as everyone, with ONE ornamented ceremonial SASH (never robes). LITERARY: a sealed Sacrificiant’s cries and speech are MUFFLED behind the cloth — emotion reads through the eyes and body. CG: the mouth-band is drawn IN on the supervising Sacrificiant for the duration of the rite.

ALIGNMENT-SENSE (the First Favored gift): they do NOT read thoughts or emotions — they perceive ALIGNMENT, how far a person’s desire, intention, sacrifice, and deepest self all point at one truth. Misalignment is as unmistakable to them as a sour note in music.

aPlot.stakesIfFail: The bond fracture becomes public, confirming Lirael's unworthiness and forcing Julian back into permanent emotional deflection
aPlot.stakesIfWin: The secret is contained and the bond realigned on terms that let both see each other without masks
aPlot.cliffhangerHook: The second thread begins to pulse, promising the next layer of who Julian truly is
aPlot.antagonistOrAntiForce: a rival vow arbiter exploiting the bond fracture for public realignment authority
aPlot.personalStakePC: her already-fragile sense of worthiness collapses if the secret confirms she was abandoned because she was unworthy
aPlot.personalStakeLI: his own wariness of vulnerability is forced into the open when the bond's true history implicates his hidden past
aPlot.pcWound: Her mother's abandonment at a young age left Lirael with a deep sense of unworthiness and distrust in relationships.
aPlot.liWound: Julian's first love left him for someone more stable, leaving him wary of vulnerability for years.
aPlot.woundSurfacingMechanism: The festival revelation of the abandonment secret drags both wounds into the open because Julian alone knows the full truth and his presence forces Lirael to decide whether to trust him with her unworthiness while his charm masks his own fear of being left again.
aPlot.woundLoadBearingProof: WOUND: The betrayal by her mother who abandoned her at a young age. CIRCUMSTANCE: The public revelation of that secret at the festival. DEPENDENCY: Without this wound, Julian would not be the one whose knowledge of the truth could either heal or deepen her distrust in relationships — his charm deflects vulnerability in the exact way her wound fears.
aPlot.liEmotionalNeedFromPC: Her capacity to need comfort without disguising it fascinates him because it creates space for him to explore his own vulnerability without fear of rejection.
aPlot.pcUnknowinglySatisfies: Despite her mask of strength she lets small moments of vulnerability show through her meaning-hungry emotional weather, which unknowingly answers his hunger for emotional honesty.
